name: Deal-Capital Network
overview: The Deal-Capital Network argues that American power is best used the way a dealmaker uses leverage: wars end when settlement pays better than fighting. Kushner's Abraham Accords are its model, normalization sold through investment and arms. Applied now, Russia is offered asset unfreezing, a Lukoil sale and energy deals for a ceasefire; Iran a negotiated end with no regime change; Venezuela an oil opening run by American firms; the Gulf chips and data centers. In its own best terms this is realism without ideology: no crusades, no forever wars, and American companies first in line for what peace builds.

The interest layer is unusually plain: the negotiators' money is foreign, and mostly Gulf. Affinity Partners reports about 99% foreign capital, led by Saudi Arabia's fund ($2B, about $25M a year in fees) with Qatari and Emirati money (Senate Finance, Jun 2024), and joined the Saudi fund's $55B Electronic Arts buyout. Aryam, Sheikh Tahnoon's vehicle, bought 49% of World Liberty for $500M. Witkoff reported about $107M in 2025 from a World Liberty-linked holding; his son Zach co-founded it, his son Alex runs the Witkoff Group, which sold the Park Lane Hotel to Qatar's fund for $623M (2023). The Trump Organization signed a Qatar golf resort with Saudi Dar Global (Apr 2025). The patrons are sovereigns, so the line tracks what Riyadh, Abu Dhabi and Doha want at the time (my reading).

Tested against acts, the 'negotiated deal' line fails on Iran and holds only in form on Russia. On Iran, Witkoff and Kushner held the Geneva talks two days before the Feb 28 strikes; Trump said on Mar 9 his decision rested on 'what Steve and Jared and Pete and others were telling me'; UK officials told the Guardian the envoys acted 'like agents of Israel' when London judged a deal close; Kushner said on Mar 26 Iran had not been serious. Only after the war reached Saudi airports and oil sites did they return as deal brokers (Islamabad Apr 25, Doha Jun 30). On Russia the deal is real but transactional: the Nov 2025 Miami plan with Putin's fund chief Dmitriev put US firms first in line for the frozen $300B, Arctic and Lukoil assets; Aryam sits in the Lukoil bid group; talks move to Abu Dhabi in mid-November; and the pressure falls on Kyiv (the refinery-strike pause Kushner asked for, Oct 29), not Moscow.

Precedent: Taft and Knox's Dollar Diplomacy (1909-13), which used American bank capital to buy influence abroad. It breaks on the direction of the money: then American capital served the state's aims; now foreign sovereign capital funds the American negotiators, so the leverage runs toward the patrons (my reading).
